summary: Took up the registered repair gap with a successor execution: the harness now adds a follower_in_live_cluster case where a three-voter cluster commits a leader-side RemoveServer, only the remaining follower is restarted while the leader keeps leading and replicating, the follower is observed after 400 ms, and the leader then appends a new configuration entry so the follower can be observed again. Local verification before submission: with the flag enabled the follower was up to date (last log index 113, last applied 110) yet held no configuration at all (latest_config_index 0, empty server set) against the two-voter entry at log index 103 in its own log, and the later configuration entry at index 114 repaired it; with the flag disabled the same follower reconstructed the two-voter configuration and was likewise repaired by that entry. Four comparisons are declared (reconstructed voter count under a live leader with its control, and the repair predicate with its control); validation reports a valid update with one experiment created and an execution requested. Incomplete: the receipt is outstanding, so no interpretation was recorded this turn, and the case does not yet exercise the voting consequence of an empty reconstruction (granting support to a peer that is not in the committed configuration).
